title: Monday 16 November summary
text:
Good morning, it is Monday 16 November: this is the GERICO summary.

Let us start with Iran. A third American aircraft carrier, the Theodore Roosevelt, has arrived in the Middle East, according to a US official quoted by Al Jazeera. Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister says Tehran will not wait to be attacked first. Reuters reports that Trump could postpone new attacks if there are no provocations.

On Ukraine, Zelensky says Ukrainian drones have neutralised more than fifty-five per cent of Russian oil refining. It is an estimate from Kyiv. He also says that restrictions on Starshield terminals allow many Russian attacks on power plants to get through. Meanwhile, China has confirmed, according to CNBC, the summit between Trump, Xi and Putin in Shenzhen on Thursday nineteen November.

Estonia is closing its border crossings with Russia following an attempted arson attack against a drone manufacturer. Tallinn attributes the operation to Russian military intelligence, while Moscow speaks of Russophobia.

In Prague, a large demonstration in support of public media: over four hundred thousand people according to ANSA, tens of thousands according to Al Jazeera. Today five European countries announce in Vienna hubs in Rwanda for rejected asylum seekers.

In Italy, amendments to the budget law must be tabled by six p.m. tomorrow. The Regions say that five hundred million for healthcare is not enough. The opposition parties have three different proposals to tax large fortunes.

The Financial Times writes that Jensen Huang is considering returning to lead Nvidia, which presents its accounts on Tuesday. The price for Anthropic's stock market offering is expected on Wednesday.

Moving on to the markets. Asia opens the week down on chips. The Nikkei loses two point zero four per cent following negative Japanese GDP data. The Kospi drops three point forty-eight per cent. US futures are down: the Nasdaq 100 loses zero point seventy-seven per cent, the S&P 500 zero point thirty-seven.

On Friday, Piazza Affari closed at fifty-one thousand eight hundred and fifty-eight points, up zero point one per cent. London gained zero point three per cent. The spread between BTPs and Bunds stands at one hundred and four basis points. On Wall Street, according to Open, the Nasdaq lost zero point eighty-two per cent and the S&P 500 zero point forty-five.

On oil, Friday's data puts Brent at ninety-six dollars and ninety-three and WTI at eighty-nine dollars and fifty-two, with Iran at the centre of tensions. Gold, on Friday morning, was worth three thousand eight hundred and ninety-eight dollars. The dollar against the yen remains above the one hundred and sixty mark. Bitcoin drops to around sixty-two thousand dollars, its lowest level in four months, according to ANSA.

There are no other high-impact events on the verified agenda for today.

The complete news stories, with sources, are on GERICO. No investment advice.
